goals.name: Achieve compliance with TMDLs issued for Steele Bayou
goals.description: The plan's overall goal is to comply with the TMDLs issued for Steele Bayou by reducing the named pollutants in the watershed.
goals.targetText: achieving compliance with TMDL's issued for Steele Bayou
goals.sourceQuote: The goals of this watershed implementation plan are geared towards achieving compliance with TMDL's issued for Steele Bayou. This can only be accomplished through the reduction of named pollutants in the watershed.

goals.name: Reach and maintain designated use for Fish and Wildlife Support
goals.description: The plan aims for Steele Bayou to reach and maintain its MDEQ designated use of Fish and Wildlife Support.
goals.targetText: reach and maintain their MDEQ designated use for Fish and Wildlife Support
goals.sourceQuote: Ultimately, Steele Bayou must reach and maintain their MDEQ designated use for Fish and Wildlife Support.

goals.name: Reduce sedimentation by 35% - 67%
goals.description: The plan expects the proposed agricultural BMPs, if properly installed and maintained, to reduce sedimentation in the watershed by 35% to 67%.
goals.sourceQuote: If installed and maintained property, the following Best Management Practices could be used to reduce sedimentation by 35% - 67% in the Steele Bayou Watershed.

goals.name: Reduce nutrients by approximately 70%
goals.description: The plan states that implementing the agricultural BMPs can reduce nutrients by about 70%, which addresses the high nutrient levels concern.
goals.targetText: nutrients can be reduced by approximately 70%
goals.sourceQuote: By implementing these BMPs, nutrients can be reduced by approximately 70% (Freedman et al. 2003, Klapproth and Johnson 2000).

goals.name: Remove fish consumption advisories for DDT and Toxaphene
goals.description: This goal is to remove the fish consumption advisories for the legacy pesticides DDT and Toxaphene. It also aims to bring water column concentrations down to the applicable human health, aquatic organism and chronic standards.
goals.targetText: removal fish consumption advisories for DDT and Toxaphene, and reduction of water column concentrations to the DDT human health and aquatic organism standard, and the Toxaphene fresh water chronic standard
goals.sourceQuote: The goal of this action item is to removal fish consumption advisories for DDT and Toxaphene, and reduction of water column concentrations to the DDT human health and aquatic organism standard, and the Toxaphene fresh water chronic standard.

goals.name: Reduction of sediment load by at least 2 tons/year
goals.description: This criterion is used to judge progress toward plan goals at the five-year assessment in 2013. It requires the sediment load to drop by at least 2 tons per year.
goals.sourceQuote: Reduction of sediment load by at least 2 tons/year, and

goals.name: Achievement of all Mississippi water quality criteria
goals.description: This progress criterion requires that all Mississippi water quality criteria be met in Steele Bayou. It is evaluated at the five-year assessment.
goals.targetText: Achievement of all Mississippi water quality criteria
goals.sourceQuote: Achievement of all Mississippi water quality criteria.

goals.name: Education strategy overall objective
goals.description: The overall aim of the education strategy is to create an atmosphere that supports sustained, long-term protection and improvement of the watershed's aquatic resources.
goals.targetText: develop an atmosphere that promotes sustained, long-term protection and improvement of aquatic resources
goals.sourceQuote: The overall objective of the education strategy in the Steele Bayou watershed is to develop an atmosphere that promotes sustained, long-term protection and improvement of aquatic resources in the watershed.

goals.name: Increase farmer and landowner awareness of the value of clean water
goals.description: An education objective to make farmers and landowners more aware of the value of clean water and of their responsibility to downstream users.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase farmer and landowner awareness of the value of clean water and their responsibility to insure others downstream have clean water.

goals.name: Increase farmer and landowner knowledge of assistance programs
goals.description: An education objective to improve farmers' and landowners' knowledge of programs that give financial or technical help with BMPs.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase farmer and landowner knowledge of programs that offer financial and/or technical assistance to plan, design, and/or install BMPs to improve water quality.

goals.name: Increase public awareness of the value of clean water
goals.description: An education objective to raise general public awareness of the value of clean water.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase public awareness of the value of clean water.

goals.name: Increase public awareness of how common activities affect water quality
goals.description: An education objective to help the public understand how everyday activities affect water quality and critical flora and fauna.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase public awareness of how common activities affect water quality and critical flora and fauna.

goals.name: Increase public awareness of how BMPs reduce negative effects
goals.description: An education objective to inform the public about how BMPs can reduce negative effects on water quality and habitat.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase public awareness of how BMPs can be used to reduce negative water quality and habitat affects.

goals.name: Increase public awareness of long term advantages of protecting water quality
goals.description: An education objective to show the public the long-term environmental and economic benefits of protecting water quality and habitat in the watershed.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase public awareness of the long term environmental and economic advantages of protecting and improving water quality and habitat in the Steele Bayou watershed.

goals.name: Increase public awareness of aquatic invasive species
goals.description: An education objective to make the public aware of aquatic invasive species and of how to prevent their accidental spread.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase public awareness of aquatic invasive species and how to prevent their accidental spread.

bmps.name: Water Control Structures
bmps.description: Agricultural water control structures to reduce sediment from adjacent cropland. A minimum of 25 units is planned at $1,500 each.

bmps.name: Large Overfall Pipes
bmps.description: Large overfall pipes (grade control) to control erosion and head cutting that delivers sediment to Steele Bayou. The cost table lists 36 units, while the BMP list on page 16 states 39 units.

bmps.name: Water Diversion Pads
bmps.description: Water diversion pads to redirect runoff and reduce erosion and sedimentation. A minimum of 1000 feet is planned at $3 per foot.

bmps.name: Bank Stabilization
bmps.description: Streambank stabilization to address bank sloughing that contributes sediment. The cost table budgets 6 units, while the BMP list says as needed with a minimum of 4.

bmps.name: Rip-Rap Weirs
bmps.description: Rip-rap weirs to control grade and trap sediment in the watershed. A minimum of 5 units is planned at $15,400 each.

bmps.name: Low water weirs
bmps.description: Low water weirs are suggested to impound more water during drought, addressing low dissolved oxygen caused by low flow and shallow water.
bmps.sourceQuote: These issues can be addressed by the installation of low water weirs to impound more water during periods of drought.

bmps.name: Riparian forest buffers
bmps.description: Riparian forest buffers are suggested to shade waters and reduce extreme water temperatures that contribute to low dissolved oxygen.
bmps.sourceQuote: Extreme water temperatures can also be mitigated by installing riparian forest buffers near waters to provide shading.

bmps.name: Herbicide (water hyacinth control)
bmps.description: Herbicide (2-4D) to chemically control water hyacinth, which blocks Steele Bayou and lowers dissolved oxygen. The Mississippi Levee Board provides the herbicide.
bmps.location: Steele Bayou Channel, Black Bayou, Main Canal

bmps.name: Herbicide Treatments
bmps.description: Herbicide application to treat water hyacinth mats, provided by the Mississippi Levee Board with assistance from Delta F.A.R.M.
bmps.location: Steele Bayou Channel, Black Bayou, Main Canal

bmps.name: Mechanical Removal of water hyacinth
bmps.description: Mechanical removal of water hyacinth, coordinated by the Mississippi Department of Transportation and the Washington County Drainage District.
bmps.location: Steele Bayou Channel, Black Bayou, Main Canal

implementation.name: Coordinate mechanical removal of water hyacinth
implementation.description: MDOT and the Washington County Drainage District will coordinate mechanical removal of water hyacinth mats blocking Steele Bayou.
implementation.responsibleParty: Mississippi Department of Transportation and the Washington County Drainage District
implementation.sourceQuote: The Mississippi Department of Transportation and the Washington County Drainage District will coordinate mechanical removal of water hyacinth.

implementation.name: Provide herbicide and application for water hyacinth treatment
implementation.description: The Mississippi Levee Board will supply herbicide and apply it to control water hyacinth, and Delta F.A.R.M. will help with application.
implementation.sourceQuote: The Mississippi Levee Board will provide herbicide and application required for treatment while Delta F.A.R.M. will provide additional assistance with application.

implementation.name: Chemical control of water hyacinth using 2-4D
implementation.description: The plan commits to chemical control of water hyacinth with 2-4D herbicide.
implementation.sourceQuote: Chemical control measures using 2-4D can and will be used.

implementation.name: Form aquatic weed work group
implementation.description: Members of MDEQ's Yazoo River Basin Team formed a work group on detection, monitoring and control of aquatic weeds, with more interagency cooperation across the Delta.
implementation.responsibleParty: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality’s Yazoo River Basin Team
implementation.sourceQuote: The severe water hyacinth problems faced on Steele Bayou have prompted members of the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality’s Yazoo River Basin Team to form a work group focused on the detection, monitoring, and control of aquatic weeds.

implementation.name: Submit funding request for silver carp project
implementation.description: Delta Wildlife and Mississippi State University submitted a funding request to the National Sea Grant Program for a project tracking silver carp movements to support harvest.
implementation.responsibleParty: Delta Wildlife and Mississippi State University
implementation.sourceQuote: To address silver carp concerns, Delta Wildlife and Mississippi State University have submitted a request for funding from the National Sea Grant Program.

implementation.name: Fisheries management plan development
implementation.description: Budgeted MDWFP task to develop a fisheries management plan for Steele Bayou.

implementation.name: Provide technical assistance to address sedimentation
implementation.description: Delta F.A.R.M., USACE, USEPA and MDEQ can give landowners technical assistance on sedimentation. Implementation depends on landowner cooperation.
implementation.responsibleParty: Delta F.A.R.M., USACE, USEPA, and MDEQ
implementation.sourceQuote: Technical assistance to address sedimentation in the Steele Bayou Watershed can be provided by Delta F.A.R.M., USACE, USEPA, and MDEQ. Implementation will be dependent on the cooperation of the private landowners.

implementation.name: Implement sediment BMPs as first action for low DO
implementation.description: To address low dissolved oxygen and organic enrichment, the first step is to install the sediment and turbidity BMPs listed earlier in the plan.
implementation.sourceQuote: Therefore, the first course of action would be to implement those BMPs listed in the previous section as addressing sediment and turbidity.

implementation.name: Five-year assessment of progress (2013)
implementation.description: Plan progress will be assessed after five years, in 2013, using water quality data, watershed activities and stakeholder concerns from 2007-2013.
implementation.sourceQuote: Progress for this watershed implementation plan will be assessed and evaluated five (5) years (2013).

implementation.name: Evaluate and revise plan
implementation.description: The plan is scheduled for evaluation and revision, organized by the Steele Bayou Implementation Team starting January 2013.
implementation.sourceQuote: This watershed implementation plan will be evaluated and revised in 2012. The evaluation of this plan will be organized by the Steele Bayou Implementation Team beginning in January 2013.

implementation.name: Develop detailed review and revision schedule
implementation.description: At the start of evaluation, the Implementation Team will draw up a detailed schedule for reviewing and revising the plan.
implementation.sourceQuote: At this time the Implementation Team will develop a detailed schedule for review and revision of this watershed implementation plan.

implementation.name: Notify stakeholders of opportunity to propose changes
implementation.description: Team members will notify their stakeholders that they can propose plan changes, with one month allowed for notification.
implementation.sourceQuote: The Implementation Team members will be responsible for notifying their stakeholders of the opportunity to propose changes to the watershed implementation plan. One month will be allowed for notification of stakeholders.

implementation.name: Evaluation and submittal of comments
implementation.description: The Team and interested stakeholders evaluate the plan and submit comments, due two months after the evaluation starts.
implementation.responsibleParty: The Team, or their designee, and any interested stakeholders
implementation.timeframe: comments will be due two months after the evaluation procedure is initiated
implementation.sourceQuote: One month will be allowed for evaluation and submittal of comments. Therefore, comments will be due two months after the evaluation procedure is initiated.

implementation.name: MDEQ prepares revised watershed implementation plan
implementation.description: After evaluation, MDEQ prepares a revised plan with the requested changes, possibly calling a meeting to reconcile conflicting comments.
implementation.sourceQuote: After evaluation, MDEQ will prepare a revised watershed implementation plan incorporating the changes requested by the reviewers. At this point it may be necessary to call a meeting to reconcile any conflicting comments or requests for change.

implementation.name: Stakeholder review of draft revised plan
implementation.description: The draft revised plan goes to the Team and commenters. Stakeholders are notified within two weeks and get one month to review.
implementation.sourceQuote: Within two weeks of receiving the draft watershed implementation plan, the Implementation Team will notify their stakeholders of the availability of the revised watershed implementation plan for stakeholder review. One month will be allowed for review of the draft.

implementation.name: Prepare and approve final watershed implementation plan
implementation.description: MDEQ prepares the final plan within a month of receiving comments and submits it to the Implementation Team for review and approval.
implementation.timeframe: Within a month after the comments on the draft watershed implementation plan are received
implementation.sourceQuote: Within a month after the comments on the draft watershed implementation plan are received, MDEQ will prepare a final watershed implementation plan. The final watershed implementation plan will be submitted to the Implementation Team for review and approval.

implementation.name: Notify stakeholders of final plan availability
implementation.description: Once the final plan is approved, the Implementation Team tells stakeholders it is complete and available as a guide for restoration and protection.
implementation.sourceQuote: After the final watershed implementation plan has been approved, the Implementation Team will notify their stakeholders of the completion and availability of the final plan for use as a guide to watershed restoration and protection activities.

monitoring.name: Dissolved Oxygen criterion (daily average)
monitoring.description: Numeric water quality criterion for dissolved oxygen in Steele Bayou perennial surface waters, expressed as a daily average minimum.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Oxygen | 5.0 mg/L daily average, 4.0 mg/L instantaneous

monitoring.name: Dissolved Oxygen criterion (instantaneous)
monitoring.description: Numeric water quality criterion for dissolved oxygen, expressed as an instantaneous minimum.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Oxygen | 5.0 mg/L daily average, 4.0 mg/L instantaneous

monitoring.name: pH criterion
monitoring.description: Water quality criterion requiring pH between 6.0 and 9.0 standard units in Steele Bayou perennial surface waters.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters

monitoring.name: Temperature criterion
monitoring.description: Maximum water temperature criterion for Steele Bayou perennial surface waters.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters

monitoring.name: Fecal coliform criterion (May–October)
monitoring.description: Summer fecal coliform criterion: geometric mean of 200 per 100 mL, with 400 per 100 mL exceeded less than 10% of the time in a 30-day period.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.frequency: geometric mean over a 30 day period, May – October
monitoring.sourceQuote: Fecal coliform | May – October: geometric mean of 200 per 100 mL, 400 per 100 mL less than ten percent (10%) of the time during a 30 day period.

monitoring.name: Fecal coliform criterion (November–April)
monitoring.description: Winter fecal coliform criterion: geometric mean of 2000 per 100 mL, with 4000 per 100 mL exceeded less than ten percent of the time in a 30-day period.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.frequency: geometric mean over a 30 day period, November – April
monitoring.sourceQuote: November – April: geometric mean of 2000 per 100 mL, 4000 per 100 mL less than ten percent of the time during a 30 day period.

monitoring.name: Specific conductance criterion
monitoring.description: Maximum specific conductance criterion for Steele Bayou perennial surface waters.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters

monitoring.name: Dissolved Solids criterion (monthly average)
monitoring.description: Maximum dissolved solids criterion expressed as a monthly average.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Solids | 750 mg/L monthly average, 1500 mg/L instantaneous

monitoring.name: Dissolved Solids criterion (instantaneous)
monitoring.description: Maximum dissolved solids criterion expressed as an instantaneous value.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou watershed perennial surface waters
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Solids | 750 mg/L monthly average, 1500 mg/L instantaneous

monitoring.name: Narrative sediment standard
monitoring.description: Mississippi's narrative water quality standard for sediment and turbidity, applied to Steele Bayou waters; no numeric value.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Mississippi’s water quality standard for sediment is narrative and reads as follows:

monitoring.name: Total nitrogen preliminary target
monitoring.description: Preliminary annual total nitrogen concentration target for west Delta water bodies, including segment MS404E of Steele Bayou, from the nutrient TMDL.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou segment MS404E (west side of the Delta)
monitoring.sourceQuote: an annual concentration of 1.05 mg/l (total nitrogen) and 0.16 mg/l (total phosphorous) are applicable targets

monitoring.name: Total phosphorus preliminary target
monitoring.description: Preliminary annual total phosphorus concentration target for west Delta water bodies, including segment MS404E of Steele Bayou, from the nutrient TMDL.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou segment MS404E (west side of the Delta)
monitoring.sourceQuote: an annual concentration of 1.05 mg/l (total nitrogen) and 0.16 mg/l (total phosphorous) are applicable targets

monitoring.name: DDT and Toxaphene water column concentrations
monitoring.description: Target to reduce water column DDT to the human health and aquatic organism standard and Toxaphene to the freshwater chronic standard, so that fish consumption advisories can be removed.
monitoring.sourceQuote: reduction of water column concentrations to the DDT human health and aquatic organism standard, and the Toxaphene fresh water chronic standard

monitoring.name: Main channel suspended sediment sampling
monitoring.description: USGS will sample suspended sediment at four bridge crossings on the Steele Bayou main channel during four storm runoff trips per year, beginning in 2008.
monitoring.location: Steele Bayou main channel at four bridge crossings
monitoring.frequency: four storm runoff trips per year, beginning in 2008
monitoring.sourceQuote: USGS will collect samples during four storm runoff trips from the main channel per year, beginning in 2008.

monitoring.name: Edge-of-field suspended sediment sampling
monitoring.description: Up to 24 discrete samples per storm trip will be collected by automatic samplers at five field edge sites where grade control structures will be installed, to assess structure efficacy.
monitoring.location: Five field edge locations with grade control structures
monitoring.frequency: each of the four storm runoff trips
monitoring.sourceQuote: Up to 24 discrete samples will be captured from the edge of field sites using automatic samplers during each of the four storm runoff trips.

monitoring.name: Stage, discharge and channel cross-section surveys
monitoring.description: Water stage recorders, discharge measurements and an annual cross-sectional survey at the four main channel sites to document sediment deposition and changes in channel morphology.
monitoring.location: Four main channel sites on Steele Bayou
monitoring.sourceQuote: Water stage recorders will be installed at the four main channel sites along with discharge measurements and annual cross-sectional survey to document sediment depositions and changes in channel morphology.

monitoring.name: Sediment load reduction progress criterion
monitoring.description: Progress criterion for the 2013 assessment: the sediment load must be reduced by at least 2 tons/year.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Reduction of sediment load by at least 2 tons/year, and

monitoring.name: Achievement of all water quality criteria
monitoring.description: Progress criterion requiring all Mississippi water quality criteria to be met in Steele Bayou by the five-year assessment.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Achievement of all Mississippi water quality criteria.

monitoring.name: Silver carp movement monitoring
monitoring.description: Proposed telemetry project to track silver carp movements in Steele Bayou and associated floodplains, so that harvest by selective traps and commercial fishermen can be increased.
monitoring.responsibleParty: Delta Wildlife and Mississippi State University
monitoring.sourceQuote: The proposed project would monitor the movements of silver carp in Steele Bayou and associated floodplains to better understand and predict their movements

outreach.name: Delta Wildlife quarterly magazine and Delta F.A.R.M. quarterly newsletter
outreach.description: Delta Wildlife and Delta F.A.R.M. regularly publish member magazines and newsletters. Part of this effort will be aimed at landowners and residents of the Steele Bayou watershed.
outreach.audience: members; landowners and residents in the watershed
outreach.sourceQuote: Delta Wildlife publishes a quarterly magazine as Delta F.AR.M. publishes a quarterly newsletter for members

outreach.name: Educational presentations at schools and to various groups
outreach.description: The organizations give educational presentations at schools and to groups. Part of this effort will target watershed landowners and residents.
outreach.sourceQuote: make educational presentations at schools and to various

outreach.name: Press releases and website outreach
outreach.description: Outreach will also be carried out through press releases and the organizations' websites.
outreach.sourceQuote: the organization will use other means of outreach through press releases and their website.

outreach.name: Implementation plan posted on organization websites
outreach.description: The watershed implementation plan will be posted online, together with information for landowners who want to take part.
outreach.sourceQuote: This implementation plan will also be available on both organization’s website along with information for landowners in the watershed who wish to participate.

outreach.name: Free bumper stickers
outreach.description: Bumper stickers will be designed and given away free to raise awareness and encourage stakeholders to take part in the plan process.
outreach.sourceQuote: Additionally, bumper stickers will be designed and offered free of charge to increase awareness and stakeholder participation in the WIP process.

outreach.name: Invasive aquatic plant signs at Steele Bayou boat ramps
outreach.description: Signs placed at Steele Bayou boat ramps will tell the public about invasive aquatic plants and how to avoid spreading them.
outreach.sourceQuote: Delta F.A.R.M. and the Issaquena County 4-H Program will be partnering to develop and place signs at Steele Bayou boat ramps that will increase the public’s awareness of invasive aquatic plants and how to reduce the risk of transport and spread.

outreach.name: Field day for 4-H high school students on aquatic invasive species
outreach.description: Delta F.A.R.M. will host a field day to teach 4-H high school students about locally occurring aquatic invasive species.
outreach.audience: high school students in the 4-H program
outreach.sourceQuote: Delta F.A.R.M. will also host a field day for high school students in the 4-H program to introduce and educate them on locally occurring aquatic invasive species.

outreach.name: Partner agency magazines/newsletters and press releases
outreach.description: Partner agencies' monthly or quarterly magazines and newsletters will carry articles to raise awareness of Steele Bayou and the plan.
outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Levee Board; MDEQ; Mississippi Bureau of Plant Industry; Mississippi's Lower Delta Partnership
outreach.sourceQuote: The Mississippi Levee Board, Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality, Mississippi Bureau of Plant Industry, and Mississippi’s Lower Delta Partnership all publish monthly or quarterly magazines/newsletters that will serve as important outlets for increasing awareness of Steele Bayou

outreach.name: Fish advisory education
outreach.description: The MDWFP Fisheries Bureau helps MDEQ educate the public about fish consumption advisories for legacy pesticides.
outreach.sourceQuote: The Fisheries Bureau of MDWFP also assists MDEQ with educational processes associated with fish advisories.

outreach.name: Stakeholder notification and comment period for plan evaluation
outreach.description: Implementation Team members will tell their stakeholders they can propose changes to the plan, allowing one month for notification and one month for comments.
outreach.sourceQuote: The Implementation Team members will be responsible for notifying their stakeholders of the opportunity to propose changes to the watershed implementation plan. One month will be allowed for notification of stakeholders.

outreach.name: Stakeholder review of draft revised plan
outreach.description: Within two weeks of receiving the draft revised plan, the Implementation Team will tell stakeholders it is available. Stakeholders then have one month to review it and comment.
outreach.timeframe: within two weeks of receiving draft; one month review
outreach.sourceQuote: Within two weeks of receiving the draft watershed implementation plan, the Implementation Team will notify their stakeholders of the availability of the revised watershed implementation plan for stakeholder review. One month will be allowed for review of the draft.

geographicAreas.name: Steele Bayou Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The watershed this implementation plan covers. It drains about 202,617 acres of the Yazoo River basin in west central Mississippi.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Steele Bayou drains approximately 202,617 acres of the Yazoo River basin in portions of Washington, Issaquena, Sharkey, and Warren counties in west central Mississippi (MDEQ 2003a).

geographicAreas.name: Yazoo River basin
geographicAreas.description: The larger river basin that contains the Steele Bayou watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Steele Bayou drains approximately 202,617 acres of the Yazoo River basin in portions of Washington, Issaquena, Sharkey, and Warren counties in west central Mississippi (MDEQ 2003a).

geographicAreas.description: One of the counties the Steele Bayou watershed lies partly within.

geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The towns of Cary and Mayersville are in the Steele Bayou watershed

geographicAreas.name: Steele Bayou segment MS404E
geographicAreas.description: The Steele Bayou segment this plan applies to. It is covered by the nutrient TMDL for large Delta rivers.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: A TMDL addressing total nitrogen and total phosphorous for selected large rivers in the Delta, including segment MS404E of Steele Bayou, has been completed and approved by U.S. EPA (MDEQ 2008).

geographicAreas.name: Black Bayou

geographicAreas.name: Main Canal
geographicAreas.description: A canal in the watershed named in the extent of the noxious aquatic vegetation concern.

geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Eagle Lake and Lake Washington are two very popular oxbow lakes in the lower Steele Bayou Watershed

geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Eagle Lake and Lake Washington are two very popular oxbow lakes in the lower Steele Bayou Watershed

geographicAreas.name: Mahannah Wildlife Management Area

geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Two popular Wildlife Management Areas (WMA’s) are located in the Watershed, Mahannah and Howard Miller.

geographicAreas.name: Howard Miller Wildlife Management Area
geographicAreas.description: A wildlife management area within the watershed, managed by MDWFP for waterfowl.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Two popular Wildlife Management Areas (WMA’s) are located in the Watershed, Mahannah and Howard Miller.

geographicAreas.name: Yazoo National Wildlife Refuge
geographicAreas.description: A refuge along Steele Bayou. Dense water hyacinth mats have blocked the bayou just south of it, which makes it a focus of the weed control effort.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Large, dense mats have completely blocked the Bayou immediately south of the Yazoo National Wildlife Refuge blocking all boat traffic
